column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2, the version a console dump holds: ResourceSizeTable.Product.100). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys), the Switch 2 SDK (sdk names its spec Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0 + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code), as Donkey Kong Bananza's.
# Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's touch layout, with rewind (D-pad down) and the Free Roam map (Y). Charge jump is holding R: the drift key
# 1.8.0 (v917504) adds subsdk1; a version packed from this profile is derived with its own shader tables (build_ipa_from_nsp.py derive_profile), so only the base game is registered
# a file of both the base game and 1.8.0 (the Product.100 table is the base game's alone: 1.8.0 has Product.180)
# From the kartnative fork, which measured them. The Switch 2's 12 GB layout gives an application a pool of 9809 MiB. nninitStartup (main+0xc387b4) sets a heap of (total - used) rounded down to
# 2 MB, less 0x60400000 (1540 MB for its other allocators), just over 8 GiB, which the heap region holds; only the pages the game touches take memory
# The 1540 MB go to its NinVirtualAddressHeap, whose free size is what the system reports free (main+0x5b1004). On Horizon the used memory counts the pages mapped in the alias region; without
# this the heap's free size never falls, and the blocks it holds were never let go (2.4 GB mapped by a fourth race, against 1.25 GB with the limit)
# agl's render buffer binding wraps its clears in render conditions in Donkey Kong Bananza (its game note): the same engine here, so they are evaluated from the start
# ---- iPhone picture and frame rate (the render-scale and present-interval stubs of patches.py, from the nxnative-mkw port of this build) ----
# The 3D views at 80 % of the game's size on the iPhone, as that port's High preset for 12 GB phones (iPhone 17 Pro, Air); the frame-rate lock stays off there (the game's own 60 / 30 choice),
# both to change in the settings screen
# The controls show when the game opens a file of its play and hide when it opens a menu's, where every touch goes to the game's touch screen. Its layouts are named for their screens:
# the race HUD (RaceInfo), the minimaps, the pause menu and the finish banner mean play; the title, the game and mode menus, the character, kart and course selects and the results mean a menu.
# The main menu draws a whole world behind its panels (1,400 to 2,400 draws a frame on an iPhone 17 Pro, as a race), so the draw count alone could not tell them apart

column1: # The user plays this port handheld at 60 fps (the iPhone, and the Mac for testing): the game starts in handheld mode
# The terrain caches (8192x8192 arrays of 68 layers, streamed by the CPU into sparse pools) hold about 2.5 GB of mapped tiles: their pages' memory goes back once uploaded
# A race went past what the iPhone 18 Pro allows (ended by the system at 7.7 GB and rising, entering a race; the Mac's race is 9.4 GB)
# ---- Memory: guest memory in a file ----
# With tex_soft's CPU uploads the 2.4 GB main pool has no zero-copy buffer, and what is left wires quickly (232 MB in 34 ms). On an iPhone 18 Pro, whose limit is 8,192 MiB, a whole
# cup ran at 3.9 GB of footprint; with guest memory anonymous a race was ended by the system at 8.17 GB
